topics.label: Course overview and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the series, outlines core concepts of cancer development, and presents the lecture learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic, environmental, and stochastic contributions to cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the core nature of cancer as a clonal genetic disease and debate the relative roles of bad luck, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens as drivers of carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections contribute to cancer, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a model of pathogen-driven oncogenesis.

topics.label: Direct and metabolically activated chemical and physical carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation, dietary mycotoxins, and chemical hydrocarbons undergo metabolic conversion to directly damage DNA through adducts, dimers, and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, chronic inflammation, and cellular susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, including chronic inflammatory promoters, the initiation versus promotion model, and host developmental stage susceptibility.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, animal, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity alongside practical risk-benefit considerations.
